title: Vox in Rama: First Papal Description of Diabolical Assembly
description: Pope Gregory IX's papal bull Vox in Rama (1233) responded to reports from Conrad of Marburg about heretics in Germany, providing the earliest papal description of a formal diabolic gathering that anticipates the later witches' sabbath. The bull described initiates kissing a toad's hindquarters, then a pale man, followed by sexual license, feasting, and the appearance of a black cat and a luminous being. Participants supposedly renounced Christ and engaged in orgiastic behavior. While directed against the Stedinger peasants and other alleged heretics, the bull's detailed description of diabolical assembly provided a template that inquisitors would elaborate over the following two centuries into the full sabbath stereotype.
historiographical_note: Norman Cohn in Europe's Inner Demons (1975) analyzed Vox in Rama as a key moment in what he called the crystallization of the stereotype — the gradual assembly of individual elements (diabolical pact, night assembly, sexual license, apostasy) into a coherent heretical sect. Richard Kieckhefer and others have traced how these papal descriptions shaped what inquisitors expected to find and therefore what torture extracted from accused.
source_method: Papal register of Gregory IX; secondary scholarship on heresy and the sabbath concept
